why: Dated, sourced availability and starter facts recorded by a person, for the cases structured automation
cannot recover reliably: a two-deep inside a game-notes PDF, a coach naming a starter at a Monday press
conference, a conference table rendered in JavaScript.
EVERY ENTRY NEEDS ALL OF: kind (AVAILABILITY|STARTER), team, player, source_name, source_url,
published_at (when the SOURCE said it), recorded_by, recorded_at, and a fixture — game_id, kickoff or
expires_at. football/availability/operator.js REFUSES anything missing one of them and publishes the
refusal, so a half-filled entry is visible rather than silently inert.
WHAT AN ENTRY CANNOT DO. It cannot declare a roster healthy: there is no 'everybody available' form,
because that is a claim about players nobody named. It cannot promote a projection to a confirmation
unless its source_url is a conference or school domain — otherwise `confirmed` is forced false and the
reason is recorded on the entry. And it cannot outrank a later official filing: reconciliation is by
